// File: use-cases/what-is-possible/options-venue

# An options venue

Onchain options are finally scaling. Notional volume hit $7.52B in Q3 2026, a two-year high, and one venue did most of it by running its own L2 with an order book and portfolio margin. That works, but it trades shared liquidity for speed: market makers hedge against spot that lives elsewhere, and collateral has to be bridged in.

Gnosis EEZ will remove that gap. A venue will be able to quote and match on 2-second blocks, then hedge, exercise or settle against mainnet spot liquidity atomically. Writers and market makers will keep one pool of capital instead of splitting inventory across chains.

The set of underlyings widens too. A venue will be able to list options on any asset with mainnet liquidity, including tokenised equities and RWAs, and hedge against L1 venues atomically rather than maintaining its own spot market.

## What we want

We want a venue that:

- Lists options on ETH, majors and tokenised equities, with RWA underlyings as a first-class market.
- Hedges and settles atomically against mainnet liquidity.
- Offers structured products that compose with L1, such as a covered call vault that keeps its collateral in a mainnet money market until it is needed.
- Reads mainnet price feeds atomically at exercise and settlement.

Source: [On-Chain Options Volume Hits a Two-Year High (Cryptorank)](https://cryptorank.io/insights/analytics/on-chain-options-volume-hits-a-two-year-high).

// File: use-cases/what-is-possible/perps-venue

# A perps venue

The best-performing perps venues today run on their own chains. They got speed, and paid for it with isolation: users bridge collateral in, liquidity bootstraps from zero, and the venue sits outside Ethereum's capital base.

Gnosis EEZ will give you app-chain performance without the app-chain trade-off. Match on 2-second blocks with sub-cent fees. Accept mainnet stablecoins and yield-bearing collateral without a bridge. Rebalance the insurance fund, hedge LP exposure or unwind a liquidation against mainnet liquidity in one atomic transaction.

Composability will also open designs a standalone chain can't support: margin that stays productive in mainnet protocols until it is called, and liquidations that route to whichever L1 venue has depth at that moment.

## What we want

We want a venue that:

- Runs a performant order book or hybrid design on 2-second blocks.
- Takes collateral straight from mainnet, with no bridge step for the user.
- Lists RWA and tokenised equity perps alongside crypto majors.
- Hedges and liquidates against mainnet spot and lending markets atomically.

// File: use-cases/what-is-possible/prediction-market

# A prediction market

Gnosis built the Conditional Tokens framework that today's largest prediction markets run on. The next design step is markets whose collateral and resolution touch L1 directly.

Prediction markets are high-frequency and small-ticket. They need fast blocks and fees that disappear into the trade, which Gnosis EEZ will deliver with 2-second blocks and sub-cent costs. What current markets have lacked is access: users bridge stablecoins in, and capital sits idle until resolution.

On Gnosis EEZ, markets will be able to settle in mainnet stablecoins without a bridge, and idle collateral will be able to sit in an L1 money market and be pulled back atomically when a trader exits. Markets will also be able to read Ethereum state directly, resolving on onchain events such as a governance vote or a protocol parameter without an oracle hop.

## What we want

We want a market that:

- Uses Conditional Tokens or a successor design, with deep liquidity on short-dated markets.
- Settles in dollars and euros, sourcing collateral from mainnet atomically.
- Resolves through credible subjective oracles, with disputes handled transparently.
- Keeps idle collateral earning on L1, withdrawn atomically when positions close.

## Apply

// File: use-cases/what-is-possible/native-infrastructure

# Native infrastructure

The four venues in this section need components designed for a chain that composes with Ethereum every slot. Existing tooling assumes a transaction lives on one chain. On Gnosis EEZ it will be able to touch two.

## Oracles

**Price feeds.** Mainnet feeds will be readable atomically, so the gap is speed and coverage: low-latency feeds that update on 2-second blocks for perps and options, and NAV and reference-rate feeds for RWA collateral.

**Subjective oracles.** Prediction markets, RWA attestations and insurance all need answers no price feed can give. We want resolution layers with clear dispute processes, that can read L1 state where an answer already lives onchain.

## Indexers

On Gnosis EEZ a single atomic transaction will be able to update state on Gnosis EEZ and on Ethereum. We want indexers and data APIs that follow those calls end to end, so a lending market can show one position across both, and a wallet can show a user's activity in one view.

## Solvers

On a standalone L2, a solver fills orders from local liquidity or holds inventory on both sides of a bridge. On Gnosis EEZ, a solver will be able to fill an L2 order against mainnet DEXs and money markets in the same transaction, with no inventory to pre-position and no settlement risk between legs. We want solvers for swaps, liquidations and intent-based orders that treat L1 and L2 liquidity as one book, including CoW Swap solvers extending batch auctions across the zone.

## Custodians

Institutions need custody that treats Gnosis EEZ and mainnet as one account, with policy engines that understand atomic cross-chain calls. We want custodians and wallet infrastructure, including Safe modules, that let a regulated business hold, move and use assets across the zone under one set of controls.

## Apply

Tell us what you are building, which request it answers, and which Gnosis EEZ attribute your product can't work without. We read everything.

// File: use-cases/what-is-possible/hybrid-apps

# Hybrid apps

Not every app needs to leave Ethereum. A mainnet protocol will be able to keep its contracts, liquidity and settlement on L1, and run its heavy or high-churn logic, such as matching or a risk engine, on Gnosis EEZ with 2-second blocks and sub-cent fees. Both halves will share one atomic transaction: both land or neither does.

Sync calls will carry a per-block verification cost on L1, so they suit high-value moments: deposit-and-use, liquidations against L1 prices and settlement. Everything else will run as ordinary Gnosis EEZ traffic. At launch, calls will run from Gnosis EEZ into L1. L1 contracts calling into Gnosis EEZ follow with bidirectional composability in 2027.

## What we want

We want mainnet teams that:

- Keep liquidity and settlement on L1 and move matching, risk or high-churn state to Gnosis EEZ.
- Reserve sync calls for high-value flows.
- Would rather build on Gnosis EEZ than operate their own sequencer, composer and prover.

## Apply

Tell us what you are building, which request it answers, and which Gnosis EEZ attribute your product can't work without. We read everything.

// File: validators/eez-transition

# Validators and node operators: the move to Gnosis EEZ

Gnosis Chain becomes Gnosis EEZ, the first instance of the [Ethereum Economic Zone](/eez), in Q1 2027. GnosisDAO has approved the transition. This page sets out what it means for the people who run the chain today: validators, and operators of RPC and archive nodes.

The short version: keep running until activation. Nothing changes before then.

## The end of Gnosis Chain as a Layer 1

Gnosis Chain continues to run as a proof-of-stake Layer 1 until the fork. At activation, its state is hard-forked onto Gnosis EEZ. Contracts, balances and addresses carry over unchanged, so the chain and its users continue. What ends is the way blocks are produced and secured.

| | Gnosis Chain today | Gnosis EEZ, after activation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block production | A proof-of-stake validator set | A composer operated by Gnosis |
| Consensus | Beacon chain, GBC | The validator set retires |
| Security | Validator economic security | Proofs verified on Ethereum |
| Node software | Execution client and consensus-layer client | Execution client only |

[Gnosis EEZ: the first instance](/eez/gnosis-eez) has the full comparison.

## Between now and activation

- **Validators keep running and keep earning.** Nothing about deposits or withdrawals changes before the fork.
- **There is no action to take** before the activation block is announced.
- **RPC and archive nodes run as they do today**, with both an execution client and a consensus-layer client.

## At activation

- **The validator set retires.** Block production moves to the composer, and blocks are proven and settled on Ethereum.
- **Staked GNO is unlocked** when the validator set sunsets.
- **GNO continues as the governance token** through GnosisDAO.

{/* TODO(ben): add the unlock mechanics for staked GNO (what validators do, if anything, to receive it, and whether it is automatic) and the timings between activation and unlock. */}

## Operating proof systems

Former validators may operate proof systems for Gnosis EEZ. Blocks on Gnosis EEZ will be accepted when a threshold of appointed proof systems agree, and proving will start with an interim setup before real-time ZK proofs. [How it works](/eez/how-it-works) describes the proving pipeline.

{/* TODO(ben): add how a former validator applies to operate a proof system, and the requirements. */}

## RPC and archive node operators

Keep your execution client. After activation, the consensus-layer client is no longer needed and can be shut down. The chain ID is not planned to change. If any network parameter changes, it will be published in the [network details](/about/networks/) before activation.

## When it happens

The launch window is Q1 2027. The activation block for the mainnet fork will be published on the [timeline](/eez/timeline) when it is set.

{/* TODO(ben): confirm where else the activation block will be announced (for example Discord, the forum or a client release), and the timings for client releases ahead of the fork. */}

## Checklist

**Validators**

- [ ] Keep your validator running until activation. Nothing changes for deposits or withdrawals.
- [ ] Watch the [timeline](/eez/timeline) for the activation block.
- [ ] At activation, expect the validator set to retire and your staked GNO to be unlocked.
- [ ] If you want to keep contributing, look at operating a proof system.

**RPC and archive node operators**

- [ ] Keep running both clients until activation.
- [ ] Watch the [timeline](/eez/timeline) for the activation block.
- [ ] After activation, keep the execution client and shut down the consensus-layer client.
- [ ] Check the [network details](/about/networks/) for any parameter changes before activation.

Other questions are answered in the [transition FAQ](/eez/faq).
